title: JSON
lede: Type-directed JSON, not a dynamic parser. JSON.stringify covers numbers, strings, booleans, uniform arrays, objects, pretty-printing, and a class toJSON() override; JSON.parse projects the parse tree onto a compile-time target type, so it needs an annotated position and refuses `any`/`unknown` dynamic shapes. The two real gaps are heterogeneous mixed-type arrays and dynamic parsing — everything else works, with a few literal-only argument restrictions on the pretty-printer.

entries.name: JSON.stringify(number)
entries.description: Serializes a number to its JSON text. Integers and floats both round-trip through the type-directed path.

entries.name: JSON.stringify(string)
entries.description: Serializes a string with the JSON escaping rules (double-quoted, embedded quotes escaped).

entries.name: JSON.stringify(number[])
entries.description: Serializes a numeric array to a JSON array. An empty array renders as [].

entries.name: JSON.stringify(string[])
entries.description: Serializes a string array, each element quoted and escaped.

entries.name: JSON.stringify(object)
entries.description: Serializes an object's fields, including nested object literals. Date fields serialize as an ISO string via their own toISOString path.

entries.name: JSON.stringify(boolean[])
entries.description: Serializes a boolean array to true/false JSON literals.
entries.snippet:
const flags: boolean[] = [true, false, true]
console.log(JSON.stringify(flags))   // [true,false,true]

entries.name: JSON.stringify(object[])
entries.description: Serializes an array of objects, each object rendered by its field set.
entries.snippet:
const points: Point[] = [{ x: 1, y: 2 }, { x: 3, y: 4 }]
console.log(JSON.stringify(points))  // [{"x":1,"y":2},{"x":3,"y":4}]

entries.name: JSON.stringify(value, null, space) — pretty-printing
entries.signature: JSON.stringify(value, null, space: number | string): string
entries.description: Pretty-prints with an indent unit and a space after each colon. A numeric space indents with N spaces; a string space is used literally as the indent unit. Empty containers stay inline even when pretty-printing.
differences: `space` must be a literal number (N spaces, capped at 10) or literal string — a runtime `space` value is a clean compile error
The `replacer` (2nd) argument is supported only as `null`/undefined — a function/array replacer is a clean compile error, not silently ignored

entries.name: JSON.stringify honors a class toJSON()
entries.description: A class with a toJSON() method serializes its result instead of its own fields, matching JS — same override dispatch as toString(). A toJSON() returning its own type is bounded against compile-time infinite recursion. Date keeps its own toISOString-based path rather than being unified.

returns.desc: The JSON of the toJSON() result.

entries.name: JSON.stringify(mixedTypeArray)
entries.description: Heterogeneous arrays aren't supported: array literals and their inferred element type are uniform-type only, so a mixed-type array has no single element type to stringify against.

entries.name: JSON.parse(s) → number
entries.description: Parses a numeric JSON string. Integers go through atoll, floats (including a float64/float32-typed variable) through strtod on the node's raw lexeme, via the type-directed projection.

entries.name: JSON.parse(s) → object
entries.statusRow: JSON.parse(s) → object (nested objects, array & object-array fields)
entries.description: Type-directed projection off the parse tree: nested objects, array-typed fields, and object-array fields (Item[]) all project through one path. A nullable-scalar field keeps its null-vs-value boxing; a missing field falls back to its type's default.

returns.desc: An instance of the annotated target type.

entries.name: JSON.parse(s) → top-level T[]
entries.statusRow: JSON.parse(s) → top-level T[] (incl. object & nested arrays)
entries.description: Projects the tree's array node into the standard {ptr,i64} aggregate, reusing the array-literal build path, including object and nested arrays.

returns.desc: The parsed array in an annotated position.

differences: A typed var-decl, an object field, and a declared-variable reassignment (`let xs: T[] = …; xs = JSON.parse(...)`) all project; a member or element target (`obj.items = JSON.parse(...)`, `grid[i] = …`) does not — assign into a variable first.

entries.name: JSON.parse(s) validates input
entries.statusRow: JSON.parse(s) validates input (throws SyntaxError on malformed JSON)
entries.description: A real recursive-descent parser builds and validates a tagged value tree. Strict JSON only (double quotes, no trailing commas/leading zeros/trailing junk), with \uXXXX + surrogate decoding and a 512-deep runtime depth guard on untrusted input. A malformed input throws a catchable SyntaxError; Response.json() inherits the same parser.

returns.desc: The parsed value, or throws SyntaxError.

differences: The `SyntaxError` message is position-based (`Unexpected token in JSON at position N`), not Node/V8's exact per-token wording

entries.name: JSON.parse(s) → any/unknown (dynamic shape)
entries.description: Dynamic-shape parsing into any/unknown isn't implemented: it needs the parse tree kept as a dynamic value, which is coupled to the dynamic object model still to come.
